summary: Wahkiakum County DNR site: 1938 40-ft wooden L-4 tower, a WWII AWS station, destroyed about 1967. Open state land, a short walk.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-ft wooden tower (1938), with a ground house
facts.status_note: Destroyed about 1967; no source describes a standing tower.

access.note: State DNR land. WillhiteWeb says no gates will stop visitors, but an active timber sale could affect access. One photo is captioned 'Blocked summit road'; the page gives no cause.

visit.trail_note: Under half a mile on foot. The paved county road ends at a major washout, and a work-around road goes around it.

facts.remains_note: A photo captioned 'Incline Footing' is credited to the web; no page says what remains on the site today.

corrections.why: WillhiteWeb and the Weebly page both say Wahkiakum County. The FFLOS and firelookout.com pages spell it Waukiakum, which looks like a misspelling of the county name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Pages describe the site from different landmarks: 2.5 miles southwest of the summit (FFLOS), 15 miles west of Castle Rock (firelookout.com), and about 9 miles southwest of Ryderwood (Weebly, citing a 1952 USGS description). The story gives the county and the access route instead of a landmark.

The Weebly page gives March 9, 1942 as the activation date. A WillhiteWeb photo caption is dated March 19, 1942. The story uses March 9, 1942, cites the Weebly page, and notes the caption date without choosing between them.

notes_for_editor: Core facts (1938 build, 40 ft, L-4 cab, destroyed about 1967) agree across all four sources. No lookout names or fire history were found in the pages read, so staffing and fire events are left out. Location: the brief's West US Lookouts coordinates (46.3089, -123.2151) were not read; the FFLOS point is kept. The county correction applies to the brief's record. The 'Incline Footing' photo is credited to the web and has no image URL recorded. One WebSearch was run and surfaced no new staffing sources.
